subject: Clarifying reserved compute bands, throughput guarantees & remedy matrix
messages:
From: Tom Harper <tharper@arborcare.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ArborCare Legal <legal@arborcare.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity: compute band mapping + remedy calc (follow-up)

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're getting our procurement team lined up and have two remaining asks before we can pull the trigger: clarity on how Redwood defines the reserved capacity bands (we call them "compute bands") and a deterministic remedy matrix if sustained throughput falls below commitment.

Specifically:
- We need a clear formula that maps our committed pool (e.g., 24 x A100 equivalents) to a contractual throughput number we can test against (requests/sec or tokens/sec) so the SREs can validate performance during acceptance.
- We'd like the remedy (service credit) calculation to be explicit and capped — procurement prefers percent-of-invoice style credits rather than operational-level KPIs that are hard to measure.
- How do burst windows/burst credits work? If we reserve N GPUs, can we burst an additional M GPUs for short windows, and how does that affect monthly billing and credits?
- Discount schedule for multi-year commits: your rep mentioned 12% for 24-month in principle; we need to see the table and whether discounts accrete with added capacity.

Can you send proposed contract wording for the capacity definition and remedy ladder? Attach the mapping spreadsheet if you have one.

Goal is to get legal comfortable so we can finalize a PO this quarter.

Thanks,
Tom Harper
Head of Platform Engineering
ArborCare Health

Attachments: none in this email

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Harper <tharper@arborcare.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: compute band mapping + remedy calc (follow-up)

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached: 1) a short mapping workbook (RC-commit-mapping.xlsx) that translates reserved GPU pool sizes into a "sustained inference throughput" (SIT) baseline for standard LLM inference patterns, and 2) a PDF with our proposed redlines for the Dedicated capacity clauses. Highlights:

Definitions we propose (contract-ready language excerpt):
- "Reserved GPU-hour (rGPUh)": one hour of a single reserved GPU instance (vendor equivalent performance normalized to Redwood reference GPU).
- "Compute Band": a named bucket (Band A/B/C) representing ranges of rGPUh per month; each band maps to a guaranteed Sustained Inference Throughput (SIT) expressed in tokens/sec and average p95 latency for a 2k-token request mix.
- "Available Throughput": the measurable SIT that Redwood provides to the customer's routes after allocation and normal maintenance windows (see exclusions).

Remedy / Service Credit matrix (proposed, excerpt):
- If ObservedSIT < 90% of CommittedSIT for the monthly billing period -> Service Credit = 10% of monthly reserved fee.
- If ObservedSIT < 75% -> Service Credit = 25% of monthly reserved fee.
- If ObservedSIT < 50% -> Service Credit = 50% of monthly reserved fee (cap).

We kept the ladder simple (percent-of-invoice) per your ask. Full clause text is in the PDF attachment; the workbook includes the mapping formulas we use (baseline token/sec per rGPUh at 512-token median sequence, occupancy assumptions, and KV-cache warmup exclusions).

Bursting: we support short-term burst capacity (up to 30% above committed pool for aggregated bursts under 24 hours/month). Bursts beyond that are billed at an overage per rGPUh. Bursts do not reset the SIT measurement for remedies (remedy uses sustained observed SIT during billing window).

Discounts: table in the workbook. Example: 12-month commit of 48 rGPUh/month -> 10% off list for Dedicated; 24-month -> 16% off list; additional volumetric bands increase discount in 5% increments. Exact schedule attached.

Next steps: Marcus can propose the legal-friendly redline tweaks Marcus: would you take the attached PDF and convert the remedy text to a short paragraph Grant-friendly clause we can accept? Dev, can you confirm the SIT measurement method in the sheet is operationally realistic?

I'll set up a 30-min sync after we have the review notes.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: RC-commit-mapping.xlsx, proposed-redlines-ArborCare-20270607.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Harper <tharper@arborcare.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: compute band mapping + remedy calc (follow-up)

Tom / Mina — quick technical note on the workbook's measurement approach so SREs understand the floor/ceiling:

Measurement details (summary):
- ObservedSIT is computed as the 95th percentile of sustained token/sec measured across all production routes that are tagged as "reserved" during the billing month. We exclude short-duration spikes (below 60s) and exclude requests served entirely from cache (cache hit >= 95% of the request) to avoid over-crediting.
- Baseline assumption in the sheet: one rGPUh (normalized to Redwood reference of 1x A100-80GB) yields ~28k tokens/sec sustained at 512-token median with 70% occupancy. Occupancy is the fraction of time the GPU is serving reserved routes vs idle/burst.
- Conversion formula included: CommittedSIT (tokens/sec) = rGPUh_pool * baseline_tokens_per_rGPUh * occupancy_factor / 3600 (to normalize per-second).

Operational notes:
- KV-cache priming and cold-starts are excluded from remediation (warmup window = first 10 minutes of any route after deploy).
- Maintenance windows: we propose monthly planned maintenance: up to 4 hours without credit. Unplanned incidents will be counted towards ObservedSIT for credit calc.

If you want, we can add a sample JMeter-like harness definition and a short test script ArborCare SREs can use to validate SIT during acceptance.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Harper <tharper@arborcare.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: compute band mapping + remedy calc (follow-up)

Tom — appreciate the pragmatic ask. A couple of contract redline edits from our side to keep the remedy deterministic and bounded:

Proposed contract-friendly wording (pricing & remedy excerpt):
"If the ObservedSIT for the billing period is less than the CommittedSIT, Customer shall receive Service Credits as follows: (i) ObservedSIT >= 90% of CommittedSIT: no credit; (ii) ObservedSIT < 90% and >= 75%: credit equal to 10% of the monthly Reserved Fee; (iii) ObservedSIT < 75% and >= 50%: credit equal to 25% of the monthly Reserved Fee; (iv) ObservedSIT < 50%: credit equal to 50% of the monthly Reserved Fee. Service Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for performance shortfalls under this Agreement and shall not exceed 50% of the monthly Reserved Fee."

On burst and overage billing: we will allow 24-hour aggregate bursts up to 30% above the pool per month without changing the committed tier; overage beyond that is billed at the per-rGPUh overage rate in the workbook. Bursts are excluded from ObservedSIT calculations for credits.

On discounts & commit amortization: we offer an early-termination adjustment if Customer terminates before term end: total committed discount will be adjusted to reflect the shorter term (pro-rated back to month of service) and any onboarding credits will be recouped. We'll add a short clause to make this formula auditable (cap on recoupment equal to 3 months of invoice).

I'll iterate the PDF to include these lines and convert the numerical ladder into a table for Legal clarity.

If these guardrails look good to you, we can ask Legal to accept the redline and then push to DocuSign.

- Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Harper <tharper@arborcare.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: compute band mapping + remedy calc (follow-up)

Mina / Marcus / Dev —

Thanks for the quick turn. The approach looks reasonable and I like the percent-of-invoice ladder. Two small asks before we hand to Legal for sign-off:

1) In the definition of "Available Throughput" can we explicitly call out that KV-cache priming (the initial 10-minute warmup per route, per your note) is excluded from ObservedSIT; please add the phrase "excluding cache warmup windows and scheduled maintenance" so there's no ambiguity.

2) For bursts: can you confirm that short bursts (under the 30%/24-hour cap) are not counted against acceptance tests during our initial 30-day acceptance window? We want to run synthetic load tests that may briefly saturate pooled GPUs.

If you can add those two clarifications to the redline PDF, we can circulate to Legal and then get a PO out. Also please upload the DocuSign-ready version when you have it.

I'll pencil in a Tuesday call to walk Legal through the ladder once we have the updated doc.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Head of Platform Engineering | ArborCare Health

Attachments: none (requested: updated redline PDF + DocuSign link)
